verdict.rationale: Adyen documents its own webhook mechanism, which pushes asynchronous status changes to a backend so it does not have to poll. Nothing in the evidence shows Agentic Commerce order lifecycle events (created, updated, fulfilled, canceled) being emitted as webhook event types. The cancel and commit session steps are calls Adyen makes to the merchant during checkout, not an order-event subscription. missing for 10: documented order lifecycle event types (created/updated/fulfilled/canceled), agentic-specific webhook subscription docs, payload schemas, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, my agent or backend can subscribe to order lifecycle events — created, updated, fulfilled, canceled — pushed programmatically

citations.quote: With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
